title: Tried Opus 5.5 for gamedev, got addicted
author: KorsAirPT
selftext:
I've been using Opus 5.5 in my company for the past months and I've noticed a large leap for coding when compared to previous models. 

I subscribed to the cheapest plan at home and tried creating a game. Within just a couple of prompts prompts got a simple FPS working. Since then I've been addicted to the iterative design and how easy it is to add new stuff and mechanics, especially once you have you start having your processes well defined. I'm having a lot of fun.

I used to do lots of small demos back in the day, even published a game for Windows Phone using an amazing framework called XNA, that Microsoft unfortunately deprecated, many, many years ago, but this it's a different world.

[Voxel Siege](https://voxelsiege.chaparrointeractive.com/) is a FPS Roguelite, inspired by Vampire Survivors (very creative I know) where a full run lasts about 25 mins. It has 6 different biomes, about 10 weapons (each with their own upgrades), loads of different passives, enemies and even some bosses.

It's available [here](https://voxelsiege.chaparrointeractive.com/).
